title: Twin Cities Marathon Returns with Record Participation
seoTitle: Twin Cities Marathon Returns, Sets New Participation.
subtitle: Event Attracts Over 30,000 Runners, Promises Pleasant October Weather
excerpt: Over 30,000 participants will gather in the Twin Cities for the 2026 marathon, setting new participation records and welcoming back defending champions.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
Over 30,000 runners will converge on the Twin Cities this weekend for the 2026 marathon, an event that has already surpassed participation records. The course, which begins at 8 AM on Sunday in downtown Minneapolis, takes athletes around lakes and concludes at the State Capitol in St. Paul.

Record Participation and Return of Champions

Organizers state that the event, which is nearly half a century old, has broken participation records. Over 30,000 people have registered for Saturday and Sunday's races. Two winners from last year, Will Norris and Jane Bareikis, return to defend their titles.

Favorable Course and Weather

Will Norris, who won last year with a time of 2 hours, 15 minutes, and 39 seconds, describes the course as "magical" and "beautiful," highlighting the experience of running around the lakes. The forecast for the weekend indicates comfortable temperatures in the 60s °F (around 15 °C).

Health Expo and Guidance for Residents

The event opens with a health and fitness expo at the St. Paul RiverCentre on Friday and Saturday afternoons. Residents of Minneapolis and St. Paul are advised to carpool, arrive early, and be aware of street closures and alternative routes.

Spectator Guide and Logistics

For those planning to cheer on the runners, Twin Cities in Motion provides a spectator guide indicating the best viewing locations, along with information on parking and street closures.

Date Change for 2027

Due to rising temperatures in recent years, organizers have decided to move the marathon to mid-October starting in 2027.

With information from MPR News.
